claims.text: A TiAlN coating is high-temperature oxidation-resistant.
Applying a thin, dense TiAlN coating will enhance the elevated-temperature mechanical performance of a titanium–nickel-based single-phase high-entropy alloy relative to the uncoated alloy.
The proposed intervention is deposition of a 1–5 µm TiAlN ceramic coating by physical vapor deposition.
The coating will form a well-adherent, continuous ceramic layer on the alloy.
The ceramic layer will act as a diffusion barrier.
The coating will reduce oxidative degradation of the alloy.
The coating will reduce surface-initiated microstructural coarsening.
The coating will inhibit surface oxidation at high temperature.
The coating will limit oxygen ingress into the alloy at high temperature.
Reduced oxidation and oxygen ingress will reduce oxidation-induced embrittlement.
Reduced oxidation and oxygen ingress will reduce microstructural degradation such as grain-boundary weakening.
Coated specimens will retain higher tensile strength than uncoated specimens in the specified high-temperature environment.
Coated specimens will exhibit better creep resistance than uncoated specimens in the specified high-temperature environment.
Coated specimens will form less oxidation scale than uncoated specimens in the specified high-temperature environment.
The proposed applicability boundary is a single-phase solid-solution high-entropy alloy in which titanium and nickel are primary components.
The targeted regime is above approximately 700 °C in oxidizing or thermally cycled environments.
